newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index tumbles in listless bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index tumbles in listless bourse trade.

text.p: German shares ended a lacklustre bourse session lower on Friday as overnight weakness on Wall Street and a touch of pre-weekend catharsis hit sentiment on the stock exchange.
The DAX index ended the session down 60.20 points, or 1,36 percent, at 4,354.15 points, while the September DAX future contract stood at 4,381 points, down 64 points.
"We've seen some profit-taking initially," said one trader.
"Volumes are quieter than they have been, and we don't see too much dramatic action. The banks are the big movers."
Bank shares were outperforming amid a fresh wave of takeover speculation which most dealers dismissed as idle chatter.
The speculation nonetheless pushed financials ahead as the so-called "silly season", when rumours fly as many market players are away on holiday, started in earnest.
Commerzbank AG, always a favourite subject of takeover talk, led volumes and traded ahead against the trend, ending at 66.55 marks, up 3.10 marks or 4.89 percent.
Various buyers were being mooted for Commerzbank, including the large Swiss banks, rival Deutsche Bank and HSBC.
Dresdner Bank was also up 50 pfennigs at 81.20 marks and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was up 1.40 marks at 98.10 marks.
Losses were otherwise spread across all sectors.
Dealers were mainly unfazed by the weakness of prices, saying this was typical of the end to a slow week.
"It's healthy to have a bit of a sell-off, but I think we may even have a bit of a rally this afternoon," said one dealer.
